builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-Rank Clebsch--Gordan Coupling for Equivariant Spherical Forecasting
summary: LCG-SFNO replaces the discretized pointwise nonlinearities of spherical Fourier neural operators, which break SO(3) equivariance through aliasing, with low-rank Clebsch-Gordan tensor-product interactions confined to a controlled low-degree band plus an exactly projected quadratic nonlinearity, implemented via a custom sparse GPU kernel (SSHCG). The cost is a specialized CUDA implementation, roughly 10 percent additional training-step time, and restriction of coupling to a low-degree band that may truncate interactions a full-bandwidth model would capture. It can fail on tasks where cross-band spectral interactions matter, on non-spherical problems where the method does not apply, and operationally if the custom kernel is not maintained against the reader's software stack.
rationale: The method is implementable on a single GPU and shows verified gains on WeatherBench, but it only matters for teams running spherical or geophysical forecasting workloads, so it should be validated on the reader's own task before adoption.
technique: Low-rank Clebsch-Gordan coupling for spherical forecasters

claims.statement: LCG-SFNO replaces the discretized pointwise nonlinearities of spherical Fourier neural operators, which break SO(3) equivariance through aliasing, with low-rank Clebsch-Gordan tensor-product interactions confined to a controlled low-degree band plus an exactly projected quadratic nonlinearity, implemented via a custom sparse GPU kernel (SSHCG). The cost is a specialized CUDA implementation, roughly 10 percent additional training-step time, and restriction of coupling to a low-degree band that may truncate interactions a full-bandwidth model would capture. It can fail on tasks where cross-band spectral interactions matter, on non-spherical problems where the method does not apply, and operationally if the custom kernel is not maintained against the reader's software stack.

Rotational equivariance error reduced to numerical precision, more than three orders of magnitude below SFNO on shallow water and five orders below it on WeatherBench, while improving forecast skill relative to SFNO on WeatherBench; the CG coupling adds about 10 percent of a training step at the operating bandwidth.
